area: wiki/dashboard-ops/index.md:36 and docs/CLOUD-WRITE-ARCHITECTURE.md:57 — the connector rule
finding: The repo states as a blanket rule that 'a routine created by an agent stores no MCP connectors'. That is false as stated. A routine inherits the connectors of the session that created it. Agent-created routines on this account fall into two groups with opposite connector states, and the distinction is what decides whether a Gmail/Calendar/CRM prompt can work at all.
evidence: list_triggers returns mcp_connections per routine, read live 2026-09-23 02:47Z across all 57 routines. The meta_mcp routines created by this ecosystem's CLI agents on 2026-09-22 (feed watchdog, Strava wrap guard, Pipeline Sync live, ISA ladder, ecosystem backup, backup verification watchdog, Weekly Loop + Self-Test) carry mcp_connections: [] — zero. The older meta_mcp batch (Real Estate Weekly Brief, Rent-Buy-Wait, Books Reconciliation, Ops Issue Review, Project Risk Review, Financial Summary, SEO Content Gap Audit, Morning Brief, Metrics Digest) each carry 11: Canva, Slack, You_com, Strava, Eromify, Notion, Claude_Code_Remote, Gmail, Context7, Google_Calendar, Composio. Steven's http_api routines carry 8-11.
fix: Both files need the qualifier: connectors are inherited from the creating session, so a meta_mcp routine may or may not have them — check mcp_connections in list_triggers rather than assuming. Neither file is in R1's ownership (routines/**, always-on/README.md), so neither was edited. The correction is written up in full in routines/cloud-routine-repairs.md under 'The hypothesis I was given, and where it is wrong'.

Both Follow Up Boss calls removed with a stated reason so they are not restored by a later reader; the CRM section is now a fixed 'not connected' sentence and substituting a Follow Up Boss figure under a Lofty label is explicitly forbidden; Calendar and Gmail kept read-only; a ciLog start/finish row pair plus a realEstateBrief document added so a dropped run is visible; a no-invention rule and a no-PII rule (counts and source health only in the database, detail to Steven in chat) added. The execution defect is NOT fixed and was not introduced here - the routine hung identically on 2026-09-21 under the old prompt - but it is now reproducible on demand. Note the durable ciLog trace added by this rewrite does not help against this failure mode, because a trace can only make a dropped run visible, not one that never started.
